Theme

Travel & transport · Household, washing & chores

accommodation noun

somewhere to stay

also accommodations, lodging, lodgings, a place to stay, put up (for the night), find somewhere to stay, quarters

classical

Cic. Att. 14.2.4: Pīliae parātum est hospitium
Cic. Sen. 84: tamquam ex hospitiō
Traupman 268: “accommodations hospitium”

hospitium, hospitiī n.

noun, second declension

lodging, a place to stay; also hospitality

First hospitality and the bond between host and guest; then the place where a guest is put up, a lodging or guest room, or an inn (Lewis & Short). hospitiō excipere, to put someone up (Hor. S. 1.5.2); in hospitia dīvidere, to billet soldiers (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dēversōrium, dēversōriī n. — an inn, a lodging on the road

    noun, second declension · also used · classical

    A place to break a journey, paid for; see hotel. The diminutive dēversōriolum is a small lodging (Cic. Att. 14.8, Lewis & Short).

  • mānsiō, mānsiōnis f. — a stay; (after Augustus) a lodging, night quarters

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 9.5.1: mānsiō Formiīs (Lewis & Short)

    In Cicero “a stay, staying on”; a dwelling or a night’s quarters only from the Augustan period on (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Pīliae parātum est hospitium, sed vellem Atticam

    a room is ready for Pilia, but I wish you would bring Attica tooCic. Att. 14.2.4

  • ex vītā ita discēdō tamquam ex hospitiō, nōn tamquam ē domō

    I leave life as one leaves a lodging, not as one leaves homeCic. Sen. 84

See also hotel, guest room, host, visitor, tenant, remain.
